testing_objectives.goal: Provide full automated test coverage across unit, integration, e2e, and security for all implemented features without leaving any function untested.

scope: Page-level UI + route handler integration through HTTP (mocked or local server)
Server actions not applicable (App Router + /api/* only)
Error handling paths and boundary rendering
WebRTC UI gating + signaling happy path (fake media devices)
Accessibility smoke checks on critical pages

security_rls.approach: Run tests against local Supabase DB to validate RLS and permissions

contract_schema.approach: Zod schema validation tests for every /api/* request/response

scripts.test:all: pnpm test:unit && pnpm test:contracts && pnpm test:integration && pnpm test:security && pnpm test:e2e

definition_of_function: Every client component with non-trivial logic

test_data_strategy.time: Use fake timers for clocks; freeze Date.now in unit/integration

unit_tests: Auth state hook: handles signed-in/signed-out transitions
Route guard utilities: redirect logic and allow-list
integration_tests: Login form submits to /api/auth/login and handles success redirect
Login error shows correct UI message
Signup form submits to /api/auth/signup and handles email verification flow if present
Protected page denies access when no session
e2e_tests: User can sign up (or sign in) and land on Play
User can sign out and is redirected
Unauthorized API call returns 401/403

unit_tests: UI selectors for invitation filtering and sorting
integration_tests: Create invitation calls /api/invites/create and updates Sent list
Sent invitations show correct state transitions after accept/decline
Accept invitation creates game and navigates to game page
Decline invitation removes/updates invite correctly
Error states: network failure, unauthorized, validation error
e2e_tests: PlayerA sends invite to PlayerB; PlayerB accepts; both enter same game
PlayerB declines invite; PlayerA sees declined status
Expired invite cannot be accepted

unit_tests: Chess state adapter: apply move updates FEN/turn
Move notation formatting (SAN/uci mapping if used)
End condition detector mapping to UI state
Persistence mapper: match row <-> domain model
integration_tests: Submitting a legal move calls /api/game/move and updates UI
Illegal move rejected and UI shows message
Game end modal appears on checkmate/stalemate
Clock stops when game finished
Resign calls /api/game/resign and updates result
e2e_tests: Two users: move by PlayerA appears for PlayerB with animation
Timeout path: force time fast-forward and verify winner
Resign flow works and game result saved

unit_tests: Bot move selection wrapper returns legal move
integration_tests: Starting bot game calls /api/bot/start and opens game
After player move, bot responds via /api/bot/move and UI updates
Bot move failure shows fallback UI
e2e_tests: User plays bot: user move triggers bot reply
Finish bot game and verify result recorded

unit_tests: Event reducer handles all event types
integration_tests: Simulated realtime event updates board state
Reconnect triggers resubscription without duplicating listeners
Out-of-order events handled safely
e2e_tests: Kill network briefly then restore; game continues and syncs
No duplicate moves after refresh

scope: Spectator chat in ongoing game view
unit_tests: Permission checks for who can send messages where
integration_tests: Player sends message -> /api/chat/send -> appears in feed
Spectator can join ongoing game chat and message appears
Unauthorized user blocked from sending
Message sanitization and max length enforced
e2e_tests: PlayerA and PlayerB chat during match
Spectator joins and chats; players see it
Spectator cannot access player-only controls

scope: Signaling via existing webrtc_rooms table + APIs
unit_tests: Role gating: only player1/player2 can initialize WebRTC
Cleanup: stop tracks, close peer connection
integration_tests: Join room calls /api/webrtc/join and transitions UI state
Offer/answer exchange through mocked API + updates state
Leave room calls /api/webrtc/leave and cleans UI
Spectator cannot call join APIs (403)
e2e_tests: Two contexts: player1 starts video and player2 connects (fake media)
Spectator sees no video controls but sees chat
Player toggles mute/camera updates UI

unit_tests: Ongoing game list sorting and filtering
Spectator mode detection and UI gating
integration_tests: Ongoing games list loads via /api/games/ongoing
Spectator opens game -> board loads and subscribes to realtime
Spectator chat works; video controls not rendered
e2e_tests: Spectator watches active match and sees moves live
Spectator posts chat message

integration_tests: Leaderboard loads from /api/leaderboard
After game finish, leaderboard reflects new ratings
Clicking username navigates correctly
e2e_tests: Leaderboard shows player and updated rating after match
Click username opens profile page

scope: Stats: ELO, games played, wins/losses/draws, streaks (if present)
Accessed via settings and leaderboard click
unit_tests: Profile data mapper from API response
Privacy rules (what is public vs private)
integration_tests: Settings -> Profile navigation works
Leaderboard click -> Profile route loads and renders stats
Profile loads from /api/profile/:id with correct caching rules
e2e_tests: Logged-in user opens own profile from settings
Visitor opens public profile from leaderboard

scope: Lesson step renderer types: explain, move_task, puzzle, quiz, model_line
unit_tests: Step type renderer router selects correct component
integration_tests: Track list loads /api/learn/tracks
Open lesson loads /api/learn/lesson/:slug and renders steps
Completing step saves progress via /api/learn/progress
Prerequisite prevents access to locked content
Practice pack runs through puzzles and records attempts
e2e_tests: User completes a beginner lesson and progress persists after refresh
User runs a practice pack and sees results summary

scope: Every route handler must have: success tests, validation tests, auth tests, permission tests, error tests

requirements.schema_validation: All routes must use Zod schemas for req/res and be tested

scope: All tables involved in features: users/profiles, matches/games, invites, chat_messages, webrtc_rooms, learn_* tables, leaderboard materialized views (if any)
tests: PlayerA can read own invites; cannot read PlayerB private invites
PlayerA can write moves only to own match
Spectator can insert chat in ongoing game only if allowed
Only players can create/join webrtc room entries
Learn progress rows only writable by owning user

integration_tests: API error renders correct empty/error state
Retry triggers refetch and success state
Offline mode disables actions
e2e_tests: Force API failure and confirm user sees recoverable message
Retry recovers after MSW flips to success

tests: Playwright + axe scan on critical pages
Keyboard-only flow: login -> play -> open modal -> close modal
Ensure game chat input is reachable and usable

scope: Board rendering does not freeze on move spam
tests: Simulate 50 moves and ensure UI remains responsive

configs: vitest.config.ts configured for Next.js + TS + coverage
msw/server.ts and msw/handlers.ts covering all /api/* endpoints
global test setup to include jest-dom and fetch polyfills
helpers: tests/fixtures/factories for users, games, invites, lessons, rooms
e2e_infra: Playwright auth storageState for playerA, playerB, spectator
Two-context helpers to run multiplayer scenarios
Fake media device setup flags for WebRTC tests

acceptance_criteria: All exported functions, hooks, route handlers, reducers, and service modules have direct tests.
All API routes have full matrix tests (success + errors + auth + permissions).
All realtime flows are validated (unit mocks + at least one E2E sync test).
All WebRTC gating is validated (unit + integration) and basic connection UI tested in E2E with fake media.
All learn track flows are tested end-to-end including progress persistence.
All leaderboard and profile navigation flows are tested and rating updates verified after a match.
RLS policy tests pass for every relevant table and role.
CI pipeline runs all tests and enforces coverage thresholds.
No flaky tests; e2e retries at most once, and failures produce trace artifacts.
